newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine c.bank sees hryvna level clear in mid-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine c.bank sees hryvna level clear in mid-Sept.

text.p: A realistic level for Ukraine's new hryvna currency, to be introduced on Monday, will emerge in the middle of September, a central bank official said on Thursday.
"The rate of the hryvna against hard currencies will show itself only when the market returns to regular functioning," Mykola Melnychuk, head of the hard currency reserves department, told Reuters.
The central bank expects commercial banks to offer more hard currency for sale in the first 10 to 20 days after the hryvna is introduced on September 2.
"We saw in the 10 or so days before the hryvna announcement a temporary rise in demand by commercial banks for the dollar, and we think the reverse trend will last just as long," he said.
The hryvna is replacing the temporary karbovanets currency, which will be withdrawn from circulation by September 16. Bank accounts will switch to the hryvna on September 2.
The announcement has not affected the karbovanets, which was unchanged at 176,100 on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Thursday.
One hryvna will be worth 100,000 karbovanets. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
